annotations.title: Get a Closed to Machines Row

description: One row of Closed to Machines, a MORVS register of which public institutions serve an automated client that names itself and gives a contact address, what their robots rules say for each path checked, and where the official route to their data is (US federal agency hosts from the Federal Register's agency list, the 50 state legislatures, the G20 members' national government portals and national law sites, and MORVS's own two hosts; checked weekly by two clients, curl and Python urllib, from one residential US vantage, both sending the same identified user agent), in full, found by query (a host, an institution's name as listed, a jurisdiction, an ISO 3166 code, or a row ID such as federal:www.usda.gov; when several match, each in short form with the arguments that return it). Returns the institution, its slice and authority (its Federal Register agency page or MORVS's curated list), the CISA .gov registry match for its domain (domain type, organisation and suborganisation; never a contact), its result class with its definition, status label, streak and class history, the robots.txt facts (status, archive hash, crawl delays, sitemaps, Content-Signal, intent-ambiguity lines and route pointers), the home-path verdict for each product token the register evaluates, grouped as training, search or user-acting (with each token's operator and whether its group follows the operator's own description), the dated checks with their responders, the route review and routes with their terms, the change-log entries for the host, and GSA Site Scanning's record for a federal host; the redacted robots excerpt when it fits. Nothing here grants permission: a robots rule is a request a site publishes, not a licence, and a page that answered certifies no deeper path. A refusal is the edge's response to this client at a stated time; the vendor named is the responder seen in headers, not the institution's policy, and no record shows a reason. "No answer" (DNS, connection, TLS or timeout) is never a refusal; none_found (reviewed, nothing found where listed) and not_reviewed are kept apart, and neither shows that no route exists. Each answer leads with uncertainty[], then as_of (the cycle date), vantage, the source page on morvs.ai and the licence, and carries the question, vantage, label, robots-not-licence and absence notes (and the self-row note for MORVS's own hosts) and the claim rules. Data more than 9 days old makes each robots verdict and next step unknown, with a note. A failed or malformed read of the register is reported as temporarily unavailable, never as an empty answer. Answers are kept under about 25 KB. Organisations only; officials appear only by office and no person is named.

query.description: Required host, institution name, jurisdiction, ISO 3166 code or row ID, for example www.usda.gov, Illinois, morvs.ai or federal:www.nsa.gov.
